summary.headline: September was a webinar-driven lead month, but SQLs fell 39% from August and 36% from last September.
summary.body: Web sessions reached 40.3K (+55% YoY) and MQLs rose to 374, led by the Source Material and Lit Talk webinars. MQL to SQL conversion dropped to 20.6% from 44.8%, and SQLs (77) and Opportunities (75) both fell about 39% MoM, which is below the seasonal norm for the back-to-school ramp. HIH reached 110, though 36 came from one Other Campaigns batch. Closed-won was $25.3K, about flat on last September, and MQA accounts stand at 99.

brand_lift.note: These are Google Search numbers, not social engagement — how often our brand and channels surface when people search. YouTube and Instagram are Search Console platform properties, visible in the Search Console UI but not exposed by the Search Analytics API, so those tiles stay blank rather than showing a fabricated zero. LinkedIn has no GSC connector — it's owned by Microsoft and isn't integrated with Google. ⏳ The week of Oct 5 is still provisional: Google has finalized only 5 of its 7 days, so its full-week total (487 branded clicks) is understated and will revise upward on the next run. The WoW figure shown compares the same 5 settled days in each week, which is the like-for-like read; the full-week comparison would be misleading until the week settles.

current.narrative: Oct 5-11: MQL (111), SQL (15) and Opp (16) all cooled off from last week's unusually high totals, though MQL is still running above its 8-week average (~71) even after the pullback. SQL and Opp fell well under their own 8-week averages (~27 each), a signal worth watching for a second week. HIH held at 32 (+14% WoW), with Inkwell (19) again the biggest driver. Disqualified (358) and Nurture (194) eased from last week's flagged spike (868/560) but are still 2.5x+ above normal levels, a second straight week of elevated list activity, still unconfirmed.

previous.narrative: Sep 28-Oct 4: a huge week for mid-funnel conversion. MQLs more than doubled to 166 (vs 76 last week), largely on the back of the Nell Duke Lit Talk webinar, which alone logged 462 recent-conversion touches. SQL (52) and Opportunities (52) each roughly tripled WoW, though product tagging on those stages is thin (only 17% carry a product tag) so the mix is hard to read yet. HIH held steady at 28 (+40%), led by Inkwell (18) and IJ (6). Separately, Disqualified (868) and Nurture (560) counts both spiked 6-11x WoW, consistent with a database cleanup sweep rather than a lead-quality drop, flagged for confirmation.
